title: Add recorded roles and a first steering role that queues work items
summary: Add a recorded role definition (A9-1, A10-1) and one first role, a steward. Every 5 finished tasks it runs in parallel and reads Athena's own state in place, adding only what would otherwise be lost. It queues work items, including one for each thing it could not see. A requirements ladder decides which things it may change itself and which it may only queue.

defaults_applied.how: One focused change: role records, one role, work item records, the ladder, and the every-5-tasks hook.
Unit and CLI tests with the fake agent; cargo test and clippy must pass.
A9/A10 and the ladder were recovered from BRIEF.md, requirements-map.md and the socratic-review ladder.
The ladder limit on self-changes is enforced in code by a path check, not by prose.
Update the requirements-map rows A9-1 and A10-1, the CHANGELOG, and the docs for an outside reader.
Reuse the existing record store, job runner and agent interface. Add no new crate.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Roles are records in athena-data: name, goal, prompt, cadence in tasks, allowed ladder rungs, with cost and yield recorded per run (A10-1).
The steward runs every 5 landed tasks as a detached job beside normal work, with no other triggers, as the addendum asks.
Work items are a new small record type, not a database. Each points at its source (job id, file, commit) instead of copying data.
Blind spots (data the steward could not read) become work items of their own.

The ladder is a small ordered set of rungs, for example: prompts and notes, then config, then code, then governance and the BRIEF. The steward may edit only the lowest rung and must queue anything above it. Rung membership is decided by path, in code.
Start small: the steward's agent run uses the existing fake or real agent interface, and tests use the fake agent.
Liberal agent permissions to start, with a short stable prompt that states the goal, as the addendum says.

acceptance_criteria.text: A role definition record type exists in athena-data (name, goal, prompt, cadence, ladder rungs allowed) and one steward role is defined with a short stable prompt.
A work item record type exists. Each item names its source by reference (job id, path or commit) and does not copy the data.
A ladder type maps a changed path to a rung. A function decides whether a role may change it itself or must queue a work item.
Run cargo test: with a fake agent, finishing the 5th task starts the steward in parallel, and the 4th does not.
Run cargo test: when a data source is unreadable, the steward queues a work item naming that blind spot.
Run cargo test: a proposed change above the role's rung is queued as a work item and is not applied.
Run cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check: both are clean.

docs/design/requirements-map.md moves rows A9-1 and A10-1 from not covered or partial to covered, naming the code. CHANGELOG.md has an entry. A short design note covers the alternatives and the ladder.

out_of_scope: Other roles (automation engineer registry A9-2, other specialists).
Triggers other than the every-N-tasks cadence.
Copying or storing logs or state that already live elsewhere.
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml, CI, or BRIEF.md beyond what is listed.
Retiring or reshaping roles automatically from cost and yield numbers.
departures: The request is broad: a new record type, a scheduler hook, a ladder and docs. I expect higher cost and time than the reference, and a lower chance of acceptance and verification.
